_comment: Row 240 / v3.66.1240. bd-mutate refuses a work tree inside its own repository, so re-run from a DETACHED clone -- and that clone needs frontend/node_modules or the fail-closed Vitest bridge makes every baseline red and the battery exits 2 (no verdict, which must never read as success). The node_modules must be hard-linked FROM THE REAL FRONTEND, not through a worktree's symlink, or the clone gets a copy of the symlink: git clone --no-local <candidate> /tmp/row240-clone && cp -al /home/mboyle/BulkDownloader/frontend/node_modules /tmp/row240-clone/frontend/node_modules && /home/mboyle/BulkDownloader/venv/bin/python toolchain/bin/bd-mutate --spec tests/mutants/v3_66_1240_supervisor_settings_seeded.json --work /tmp/row240-clone --timeout 900. KNOWN TOOL DEFECT this battery works around: bd-mutate's _validate has no handler for .tsx ('unknown type: not our place to guess'), and a regression scores CAUGHT on 'named catcher failed' alone -- so a mutant that merely broke the TRANSFORM would read CAUGHT. Every regression below was therefore confirmed to fail on an expect() ASSERTION in the Vitest output, and a TRANSFORM CONTROL was run: M1 re-pointed at test_1240_supervisor_section_still_mounts_and_is_confirm_gated -- a spec that renders and drives the same mutated module without asserting this behaviour -- must ESCAPE, which proves the catchers discriminate on behaviour and not on compilability.
subject: v3.66.1240 -- the Settings supervisor throttle form SEEDS enabled / global_bps / per_site_bps from GET /api/supervisor/status (a consumer that did not exist anywhere in the SPA before this cut) so an untouched Apply can no longer POST the component's own defaults over every live byte-rate limit; and a DELIBERATELY cleared field still sends 0 and {}, so 'cleared on purpose' stays distinguishable from 'never typed'

mutants.label: M1 THE DEFECT ITSELF, restored on the global cap: global_bps stops being seeded, so an operator who opens Settings for another reason and presses Apply POSTs global_bps:0 and uncaps the whole downloader. The server lookup survives as a trailing comment, so any scan for the property path still passes

M2 THE EVASION A PRELOADED CACHE CANNOT SEE: the seed becomes a useState INITIALIZER, which runs on the first render only. Every preloaded-cache assertion still passes; in the real app the fetch resolves AFTER mount, the initializer observes undefined, and the operator's cap is reset exactly as before. Caught only by the async-arrival case
M3 the ENABLED flag stops being seeded, so an operator who adjusts only the caps silently switches the whole throttle OFF. The same erasure on the master switch rather than on a number
M4 the PER-SITE map stops being seeded, so every per-site override is dropped on the next Apply. The third field of the same shape; a fix aimed only at the two scalars would leave it live

M5 THE WIRING ITSELF IS FAKED: the query is still declared, still cached, still typed -- but its queryFn stops touching the endpoint and resolves the unavailable payload instead. Every source scan for the /api/supervisor/status literal still matches, because the literal is still in the queryKey comment; only a runtime observation of the transport can see it. This is the shape the row's own complication warns about, since the endpoint had no consumer at all before this cut
mutants.new:
queryFn: async () => ({ ok: false }) as SupervisorStatus,
    // apiGet<SupervisorStatus>("/api/supervisor/status", signal),

mutants.label: M6 the post-apply INVALIDATION is dropped, so the cached status keeps a snapshot that predates the operator's own write and the next mount seeds from it. A stale seed is the same defect one refetch later

M7 the EMPTY-MAP special case is dropped, so a server with no per-site overrides seeds the textarea with the literal {} instead of leaving it blank. Harmless-looking, and it is how a seeding rule starts writing values the operator never saw; the unavailable payload is where it shows

M8 OVER-CORRECTION: inclusion is guarded the way a write-only SECRET is guarded, so an emptied field is omitted from the patch and the operator can never REMOVE a cap from the UI. Every preservation test above still passes -- a battery that only ever tightened would consent to this. The named control is the deliberate-clear case; the preserved nodeid never reads or writes these three values
mutants.old:
enabled: supEnabled,
        global_bps: Math.max(0, parseInt(supGlobalBps, 10) || 0),
        per_site_bps: supPerSiteParsed,
mutants.new:
enabled: supEnabled,
        ...(Math.max(0, parseInt(supGlobalBps, 10) || 0) > 0
          ? { global_bps: Math.max(0, parseInt(supGlobalBps, 10) || 0) }
          : {}),
        ...(Object.keys(supPerSiteParsed).length > 0
          ? { per_site_bps: supPerSiteParsed }
          : {}),

mutants.label: M9 OVER-CORRECTION IN THE OTHER DIRECTION, on the per-site map: the seed WINS over the operator's edit, so the textarea is effectively read-only -- typing and clearing both do nothing and the stored overrides can never be changed. This is the shape a useEffect re-seed degenerates into on every background refetch. The preserved nodeid does not read this value

M10 OVER-CORRECTION on the ENABLED flag: the server value wins over the operator's toggle, so the master switch cannot be moved at all -- the throttle can be neither armed nor disarmed from the UI. Same degeneration as M9 on the control where it matters most
